summary: Yasuro Abe specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako University and served as a professor at Nagoya University (~2003–2019) and Osaka University (attested 2004), alongside a post at Otemae University.

Yasutaka Muroya works in Indology and philosophy. He served as a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and Leipzig University (attested 2015), and as a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami specializes in Buddhist studies. Educated at Tohoku University, he held posts at Koyasan University and Yamaguchi University, and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).
Yi-hsun Huang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner, and later taught Huidi Zeng.

Yifa works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at National Taiwan University, the University of Hawaii, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein, and trained under Hsing Yun. She taught at the University of the West (~1996–2004) and visited Harvard (2001–2002).

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1994–1999) under Sheldon Pollock. He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2009) and taught Roy Tzohar.

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fu Jen, Yenching, and Harvard, studying under Yinke Chen (~1935–1939). Zhou served as a professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).

Yin Shun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu (~1931–1947), at Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, and Taisho University. He held posts at Minnan, Wuchang, Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

Ying-shih Yü worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at CUHK, Kansai University, and Harvard, he held professorships at the University of Michigan (~1962–1966), Yale University (~1977–1987), and Princeton University (~1987–2021).
Yingguang Qu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Nordan Hutuktu in 1926 and under Bai Puren in 1929.

Yinke Chen worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fudan, Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard. He held posts at Tsinghua (~1926–1937), Peking University (~1946–1948), and Sun Yat-sen University (~1949–1969).
Yiu Wing Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong by 2013, supervised by K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yiu-ming Fung specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1984) and served as Acting Head of the Division of Humanities at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2008–2009).

Yohei Kawajiri is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and a special researcher with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and served as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003, 2015).
Yong Hua Shi works in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (~1988), Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1994–1999), and Trulshik Rinpoche, and taught Cortland Dahl and Adam Pearcey.
Yongshan He specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, and was also taught by Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1911–1917) and Harvard University (~1919–1922), and held a position in the Philosophy Department at Peking University in 1949.
